summary:
BIOORBIT is a web-based crew health command dashboard for astronauts on cislunar and deep-space missions. It tracks each crew member’s vitals live (heart rate, blood pressure, SpO₂, temperature, respiration, HRV) against safe ranges. It raises severity-ranked alerts that can be acknowledged. It also follows longer-term indicators such as radiation dose, sleep, alertness, stress and muscle loss, with a 30/60/90-day health improvement graph. Mission eligibility checks, personalised daily routines, shift handover, scenario simulation, CSV export and PDF medical records support flight surgeons. An AI Flight Surgeon assistant helps interpret the data.

It addresses the challenge by giving crews and ground teams one place to detect early physiological decline. Far from Earth, real-time medical help is delayed or unavailable, so spotting problems early and acting on them autonomously becomes critical. It matters because astronaut health is the limiting factor for Moon and Mars missions, and tools like this make longer, safer exploration possible.
details:
BIOORBIT is a browser-based crew health command centre for long-duration missions such as Lunar Gateway, lunar surface and Mars transit. It shows each astronaut’s live vitals (heart rate, blood pressure, SpO₂, temperature, respiration, HRV) against safe-range bands. It also tracks radiation dose, sleep and fatigue, bone and muscle loss, and mental health indicators across 30/60/90-day trends and a 0-100 health score. When a reading crosses a threshold, it raises severity-ranked alerts that crew or ground teams can acknowledge. Scenario simulations (tachycardia, hypoxia, fever, hypertension, acute stress) let teams rehearse responses. The app also includes mission eligibility checks, personalised daily routines, shift handover, a crew log, CSV export and PDF medical records. An AI Flight Surgeon assistant, usable by typing or voice, explains the data and suggests next steps.

Benefits and intended impact

Far from Earth, communication delays and limited medical staff mean problems must be caught early and handled autonomously. BIOORBIT puts all health data in one place and turns raw numbers into clear, actionable status. The goal is safer, longer missions and less workload for crew and flight surgeons.

Tools and technologies

HTML, CSS and JavaScript in a single self-contained file, with Tailwind CSS, Lucide icons, SVG and Canvas charts, the Web Speech API for voice, the Web Audio API for alert sounds, and localStorage for saved data. The AI Surgeon connects to Claude, Gemini, OpenAI, OpenRouter or any OpenAI-compatible API using the user’s own key. Health context draws on NASA HRP, the Twins Study, NASA OSDR and ESA HREDA. The vitals in this prototype are simulated.

Creativity

It has a Holo Lab holographic projection bay, voice-controlled commands such as “set environment to Mars”, and a built-in model of the 1.3 s Earth–Gateway light delay. It has no backend and nothing to install.

Factors considered

Realistic clinical thresholds, communication delay and crew autonomy, privacy (data stays on the device), usability under stress, and honest labelling of simulated data.
